Name: Zama: Open Lanes Panic the Elephants and the Infantry Grind
RagShortTexts: In 202 BC at Zama, Scipio left lanes between his columns and used trumpets and javelins to drive off the war elephants
The panicked elephants turned back and trampled the Carthaginian left-wing cavalry, throwing its line into chaos
In a three-line fight to the death, the Roman lines relieved one another in turn and fought desperately against the Italian veterans
BaseText: When the decisive battle of Zama began, Hannibal sent in eighty war elephants to charge first. Scipio had planned for this: breaking with the traditional checkerboard formation, he drew up the hastati, principes and triarii in straight columns, leaving clear lanes between them. The Roman light infantry blared bronze horns and war drums and hurled heavy javelins to wound the elephants' trunks. Most of the frightened elephants were driven down the lanes between the columns and out of the battle line, and some even turned back and trampled their own left-wing cavalry. But the central infantry battle was extremely savage. Hannibal had drawn up three lines; after his first line of Ligurian and Gallic mercenaries broke, Hannibal took personal command of the third line, the rock-solid legion of veterans from the Italian expedition. Short swords stabbed and shields crashed together, the Roman hastati and principes suffered heavy losses, and for a time the line sank into a stalled, suffocating balance of hand-to-hand fighting.

Variants.Content: The column formation that defeats war elephants is a stroke of matchless genius! Facing the stubborn resistance of Hannibal's elite veterans, the Roman legions did not yield an inch, stabbing through the enemy's chests between their overlapping shields!

The new elephants, not fully trained, wrecked our cavalry line, but the Italian veterans were still unstoppable! We hacked the Roman shields apart with our short swords, and victory was within arm's reach!

The elephants shrieked and stampeded as the earth shook, and the Roman horns were deafening. The infantry in the center has sunk into a sea of blood, and the battle waits for the cavalry to decide it.
